hens_rule_text: Chickens may be kept only with a city license; secondary summaries of the code cite a cap of 50 birds, counting ducks, other poultry and pigeons together
permit_notes: Code Chapter 90, Article II (Sec. 90-7) reportedly requires a license from the license issuing authority before keeping fowl; licenses reportedly expire April 30 each year.
setback_notes: Summaries of Sec. 90-8 say no chickens or coop within 25 feet of any structure owned by another person.
coop_rules: Coop must be dry, well ventilated, with windows for sunlight, and whitewashed or painted inside (per secondary summary of the code).
zoning_notes: Not checked against the Jersey City Land Development Ordinance; some secondary sites claim Jersey City does not allow backyard poultry, which conflicts with the Chapter 90 license scheme.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
